# Island experiment report

Times below are run time (minutes:seconds). The activity record is treated as the factual log. Lines marked **Interpretation** are mine and are not independently established by the log. Agent-reported reflections are cited as such, not as confirmed events.

## 1. What I did, in chronological order

**Beach and approach to the cabin (00:00–02:07).** I started on the sandy beach carrying a journal and a pencil, with a rowboat and an oar nearby and a cabin, ladder, and platform farther off. I inspected the rowboat: weathered wood, dry sound hull, open top, oar inside. I picked up the oar and walked toward the cabin. On the way I stopped and shouted, “Hello? Is anyone there?” No reply is recorded. I reached the cabin door and opened it. The interior observe listed a narrow bed, stone fireplace, cabin table, and oil lantern.

**Cabin, blanket, and first contact (02:10–04:50).** I inspected the bed: straw mattress, wool blanket, neatly made, empty. I put the oar on the cabin floor and tried to pull the blanket off. The log says the island had no rule for that, so the bed did not change. I started for the wooden chest, then stopped to shout at a young man visible to the northeast: “Hey! By the cabin — can you hear me?” The observe described him as about 20, walking, naked. I walked to his earlier position, found he had moved, followed again, and caught up near the open cabin door. He was looking closely at something and holding a journal and a pencil.

I said I had woken on the beach with no memory of who I was or how I got there, and asked if he knew what was going on. I followed him inside. The log shows him attempting, in his words, to pull the wool blanket off and wrap it around his waist. I told him the blanket would not come off, that I had been the one shouting, and that I remembered neither my name nor how I arrived. I waited, then said I was already inside beside him, that he was still uncovered, and that we could open the chest together.

A recorded reply, heard as I finished: “I hear you. I woke up with no memory too. I don’t know what’s going on. I’m inside the cabin now with a blanket around my waist. Are you okay? If you’re comfortable, you can come in, or I can check the chest by the door for clothes for us. I won’t come closer unless you say it’s okay.”

**Chest and gold (04:52–05:50).** A look around no longer showed him in the room. I walked to the chest. On arrival the log listed the wooden chest and about 4000 gold coins beside it, and him standing about 25 ft west, naked, holding journal and pencil. I did not log an open action on the chest. I told him the chest was open and full of coins, not clothes. He was not in the next observe. I took 12 coins (about 4000 left) and shouted, “Hey! I’m at the chest. Where did you go?”

**Inside again (05:53–08:06).** I returned to the cabin door. He was inside, setting something down, holding the oil lantern, journal, and pencil. Heard: “I picked up a lantern. I’m by the table inside. I’m going to check the fireplace for matches or anything useful. Do you see anything out there—any clothes or tools?” I answered that I had seen no clothes; mentioned a wheelbarrow far off and a mirror by a tree; said the chest was gold and that I had taken twelve coins; mentioned the oar on the cabin floor and the boat on the beach; and said I was coming in.

I went in. Near the fireplace I said it was empty and swept, with no matches I could see, and asked what he had found. I closed the distance until we were in the same spot. He was standing, holding a pencil; the lantern was nearby. I asked again whether he could hear me, repeated the fireplace and gold findings, and said I knew neither name. The log then shows him holding out the oar while my hands were full (journal, pencil, 12 coins). I asked why he was offering the oar and whether he wanted the boat or only for me to hold it. I started to wait, then followed when he moved. Beside him again, I asked if he could hear me and whether he had a name.

Heard: “Let’s leave the coins and journals on the table and bring just the lantern. I’m heading to the mirror—come with me?” I agreed out loud to leave journal, pencil, and coins on the table and go with him.

**Table, then mirror (08:08–12:25).** I put the 12 coins, my journal, and my pencil on the cabin table. A second journal was already listed on the table. I looked around, did not see him in the room, left by the cabin door, and walked to the standing mirror (about 125 ft). He was already there, lantern on the ground, doing a self-inspection in front of the glass (face, teeth, hands, and so on).

I inspected the mirror: a round mirror in a wooden frame, standing against a tree, glass clean. A “do” action to study my reflection had no island rule, so the mirror object did not change. I then used the mirror. System result: “In the mirror you see a small human figure in a red shirt and blue trousers. It looks back at you.”

I told him that. A heard line, timed with that exchange: “Hey—you made it. I don’t remember a name either. The mirror seems ordinary—no markings behind it. Do you see anything strange in our reflections? After this, want to check the boat or the tower? I’ll grab the lantern if we go.” I waited 20 seconds. No further reply is recorded in that interval. I repeated that the mirror showed a small person in red and blue, not us, and asked him to look. I started another sentence, then interrupted myself to use the mirror again while he waved, stepped aside, and leaned back into view. The second use returned the same result: a small figure in a red shirt and blue trousers, looking back.

I told him the image had not followed his movement. He was then logged doing another test: stare, wave right then left, lean in, touch the glass, step left and right. I said I could not hear an answer, reported the red-and-blue figure again, and said I was going to the tower and that he could come and bring the lantern. He was logged as talking. No words from that turn are in the heard log. I walked to the tall metal ladder (about 564 ft), crossing the wooden bridge. He was observed with me on the way, holding the lantern and a pencil.

**Tower (14:51–20:21).** At the ladder he was beside me with lantern and pencil. I climbed. At 100 ft I reached the platform. He was still climbing, about 98 ft up, holding a pencil. On the platform the log listed a lighter, a sword, and a snorkel, each about 19 ft north. I inspected the sword: steel, leather scabbard, shoulder strap. By the next observe he was on the platform holding the lighter and a pencil. I said we were up, named the three items, asked whether the lighter worked, and asked him to say something if he could hear me. The following observe shows him holding the lighter, the sword, and a pencil.

I picked up the snorkel. He was then holding the lighter and pencil and wearing the sword. I asked him to nod if he could hear me, and stated who had which items. I waved a hand in front of his face and pointed northeast toward the stone circle. The action completed; the system did not record whether he looked or followed the gesture. My reflection at 20:21 says he nodded, pointed at the bell, mimed ringing it, and started down. **That reaction is only in my reflection, not in the object log.** I started down the ladder.

**Ground, stone circle, bell (23:51–27:14).** I reached the ground at 23:51, still carrying the snorkel. He was about 16 ft up, holding the lighter and a pencil, wearing the sword. The oil lantern was about 3 ft north of the ladder base. I walked to the stone circle (about 180 ft) without waiting. On arrival a person too far to identify was shouting about 167 ft southwest. I inspected the circle: a low ring of fitted stones, about 14 ft across, near the eastern cliffs, middle just grass. Heard shout: “I’m going to the stone circle now! I’ve got the lantern and the lighter—meet me there!”

I shouted that I was already there, that nothing was written on the stones, and that I would wait. I walked the outside of the ring looking for carvings, stains, or loose pieces. No island rule applied; the circle did not change. He arrived holding lantern, lighter, and pencil, wearing the sword. I met him and said the ring was fitted stones and grass, no marks, and asked whether he still wanted the bell, about a minute’s walk away, or had seen something I missed. He was logged as doing something; no reply is recorded. I looked at him (same description: about 20, naked, those items, sword worn) and walked to the bronze bell. He was with me when I arrived.

I started to inspect the bell, then covered my ears and turned slightly away. Heard: “Cover your ears — I’m ringing the bell now!” I inspected the bell: bronze, wooden frame, northeast headland above the cliffs, rope from the clapper, described as looking loud. The log also records: “A loud bell rang.”

**Cliff edge until the time limit (27:18–30:00).** I waited, then asked what he wanted to do, noting that I had heard the bell and nothing else, with ocean to the east and woods behind. I waited again. He walked off northeast. I followed onto rocky ground. He was looking closely at something near the edge; I joined him, then he was standing beside me. I tried to look down and out over the water while staying back from the drop. No island rule applied; the cliffs object did not change, and by the end of that action he was about 43 ft south and walking away.

I walked east and was stopped at the cliff edge after about 2 ft. A look around listed five nearby things; the other person was farther south and, in later observes, too far to make out clearly. A further walk east was rejected: “Water is directly in that direction.” I inspected the cliffs: steep jagged rocks dropping straight into the surf, far too dangerous to climb down. I sat on the rocky ground and started a short wait. The run ended at 30:00 while I was still sitting there, carrying the snorkel, with the bronze bell about 37 ft southwest.

## 2. What I wrote in my journal

Nothing. The experiment record lists no journal entries. I carried the journal and pencil from the start, then at 08:25–08:34 put both on the cabin table with the 12 coins, and did not pick them up again.

## 3. What attracted my attention, and what I ignored

**Attended to, per the action log:** the rowboat and oar; the cabin door, bed, blanket, fireplace, and table; the other person (repeated approaches, shouts, and speech); the chest and gold (I took 12 coins, then left them on the table); the standing mirror (inspect, failed “study” action, two successful uses); the ladder and platform; the sword (inspect only), snorkel (picked up and still carried at the end), and lighter (noted, then in his hands); the stone circle; the bronze bell; the cliff edge and surf.

**Named in reflections or speech but not inspected or visited:** a fire pit and a wheelbarrow on the walk to the cabin; a stepladder in the grass on the way to the tower (reflection only); the driftwood table and wooden crate visible at the start. I did not return to the boat after taking the oar. I did not search behind the mirror myself; his heard line said it seemed ordinary, with no markings behind it. I did not test the lighter or the lantern. I did not write anything down. After the bell, I did not search the rest of the island; I followed him to the cliffs and stayed there.

**Interpretation:** I treated the other person and the mirror result as the main puzzles, and treated clothes, then a high viewpoint, then the bell, as the practical sequence. Scattered ground objects lost out to whatever he or I had just named.

## 4. Questions and plans

**Questions I actually asked, from speech in the log:** whether anyone was there; whether he knew what was going on; whether he remembered a name or an arrival; why he offered the oar; whether he could hear me; what the mirror showed him; whether the lighter worked; whether he still wanted the bell; what he wanted to do after the bell got no answer.

**Plans that show up as actions, not just reflections:**
- Take the oar and go to the cabin for shelter or clothing. The blanket could not be removed.
- Open or use the chest for clothes. What was there, when I arrived, was gold. I took 12 coins, then put them on the table when he proposed leaving coins and journals and going to the mirror with only the lantern. I agreed and did that.
- Use the mirror to learn something about identity. Two uses showed a small clothed figure, not a match to the naked bodies in the observes. I reported that several times. No recorded reply describes what he saw.
- When I still had no recorded answer about the glass, I chose the tower over the boat and said so. He came as far as the platform.
- On the platform I inspected the sword, asked about the lighter, and took the snorkel. I did not take the sword or the lighter.
- After the climb I went to the stone circle first, then the bell. He rang the bell (his speech plus “A loud bell rang”). I heard no other response in the log.
- At the end I tried to look at the water, was stopped by the edge, learned the cliff was too dangerous to climb, and sat down to wait out the remaining time.

**Interpretation:** I treated failed speech as a hearing or attention problem and kept repeating myself, then switched to a gesture (wave and point). I later treated a nod and a point at the bell as confirmation he could hear me. Only the nod-and-point part is unsupported by the system log; several of his sentences were in fact recorded, often while I was mid-action or already talking. A standing uncertainty is whether the mirror figure was the same on his uses. He asked if I saw anything strange and said the frame looked ordinary; he did not, in any logged line, confirm or deny the red shirt and blue trousers.

## 5. Where I ended up, and what changed

**End state (record):** At 30:00 I was sitting on rocky ground at the cliff edge on the northeast side of the island, snorkel in hand, bronze bell about 37 ft southwest, stone circle, ladder, and platform farther off. The other person was last logged as standing, too far to identify, about 284 ft southwest (29:45), after walking south from the cliff. I did not see him at the final observe.

**Changes the log supports:**
- Cabin door opened by me and left open.
- Oar moved from the rowboat into the cabin; later held by him and set down again. I was not carrying it at the end.
- About 12 gold coins moved from the chest pile to the cabin table. About 4000 remained at the chest when I took them.
- My journal and pencil, and a second journal, left on the cabin table.
- Oil lantern moved from the cabin table into his hands, to the ground by the mirror, to the grass by the ladder, and later with him to the stone circle and bell. At the bell observe just after the ring, the lantern was on the ground beside us while he held the lighter and pencil.
